problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+2\sqrt{2}\,t\,k$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
{{field-1}}
$i\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t$

$j$
worked_solution:
First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{2}\,t)\,k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+2\sqrt{2}\,k \\  \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+8} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+2\sqrt{2}\,k}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i-\frac{1}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2})\,k \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+0\,k \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\  \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{9}({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$
